summary: Resolving a title to a TMDb id is a ranked guess, not a lookup: when several entries share the title, the CLI must name the runners-up on stderr and accept a year to override, never silently take the most popular one.
reason: TMDb orders /search/* by current popularity, so a remake outranks a better-rated original — `ratings "Sabrina"` returned the 1995 version (703 ratings) over the 1954 Wilder film (1373 ratings) with nothing in stdout, stderr, or the exit code to show a choice had been made. Any regen that restores a bare Results[0] pick reintroduces a wrong answer that reads as a confident one. The notice must stay on stderr so the stdout JSON contract, --agent, --select, and pipes are untouched, and it must be gated on rating counts: TMDb's long tail of unrated same-titled shorts otherwise makes it fire on every lookup, which is the same as not having it.
validated_outcome: Live TMDb: `ratings "Sabrina"` now prints the 1954 and 2018 alternatives on stderr while stdout stays valid --agent JSON; `--year 1954`, `"Sabrina (1954)"`, and `versus "Sabrina (1954)" "Sabrina (1995)"` all resolve to the intended ids; `ratings "Inception"`, `"Fight Club"`, `"The Matrix"`, and `"Heat"` stay silent; `--quiet` suppresses the notice. go build/vet/test and the repo verify-skill checks pass.
